title: Security+ SY0-701 — wireless security (help-desk precursor)
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 objectives (wireless security standards; attacks; 802.1X/PSK; site survey; Bluetooth risks)

terms.title: SSID
terms.definition: Service set identifier — the network name a wireless network advertises (or tries to hide).
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — SSID / wireless basics

terms.title: WEP
terms.definition: Wired Equivalent Privacy — obsolete Wi-Fi encryption that is easily broken; treat as insecure legacy.

terms.title: WPA2
terms.definition: Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 — widely deployed Wi-Fi security using strong encryption (AES-CCMP) when configured correctly.

terms.title: WPA3
terms.definition: Newer Wi-Fi security standard with stronger protections (including SAE) against offline password attacks and better open-network options.

terms.title: SAE
terms.definition: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals — WPA3 handshake that resists offline dictionary attacks better than WPA2-PSK.

terms.title: PSK (pre-shared key)
terms.definition: Shared Wi-Fi password mode — everyone uses the same key; fine for small spaces, weak for accountability and rotation.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — PSK / personal mode

terms.title: WPA-Enterprise (802.1X)
terms.definition: Wi-Fi that authenticates each user/device via 802.1X (usually RADIUS) instead of one shared password.

terms.title: 802.1X
terms.definition: Port-based network access control — authenticate before full network access; used for enterprise Wi-Fi and wired NAC.

terms.title: RADIUS
terms.definition: Authentication server protocol commonly behind enterprise Wi-Fi — checks user/device credentials for 802.1X.

terms.title: Open network
terms.definition: Wi-Fi with no encryption on the air — anyone nearby can join and often eavesdrop unless a higher layer protects traffic.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — open / insecure wireless

terms.title: Captive portal
terms.definition: Web login/splash page before internet access — common on guest Wi-Fi; not a substitute for strong link encryption by itself.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — captive portal / guest access

terms.title: WPS
terms.definition: Wi-Fi Protected Setup — convenience pairing feature with a history of brute-force weaknesses; disable when possible.

terms.title: Evil twin
terms.definition: Attacker access point that mimics a trusted SSID to trick clients into connecting and exposing traffic or credentials.

terms.title: Rogue access point
terms.definition: Unauthorized AP on the network or in range — intentional attack gear or a well-meaning employee 'helping' coverage.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — rogue access point

terms.title: Disassociation / deauthentication
terms.definition: Wireless frames that kick clients off an AP — used in DoS or to force reconnects toward an evil twin.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — disassociation / deauthentication attacks

terms.title: Jamming
terms.definition: Flooding RF so legitimate Wi-Fi cannot communicate — a denial-of-service against the air itself.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — jamming / RF interference (attack)

terms.title: War driving
terms.definition: Roaming an area to discover and map Wi-Fi networks — often looking for weak or open targets.

terms.title: Wireless eavesdropping
terms.definition: Capturing Wi-Fi frames from the air — catastrophic on open/WEP, still a concern if clients join the wrong network.

terms.title: Replay attack
terms.definition: Capturing valid wireless or auth traffic and re-sending it later to gain access or disrupt sessions.

terms.title: IV attack (WEP)
terms.definition: Exploiting WEP's weak initialization vectors to recover the key — one reason WEP is retired.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — IV attack / WEP weaknesses

terms.title: Site survey
terms.definition: Measuring coverage, interference, and dead zones so APs are placed and tuned for both performance and security boundaries.

terms.title: Guest Wi-Fi
terms.definition: Separate wireless access for visitors — should not freely reach internal servers or employee laptops.

terms.title: Network segmentation
terms.definition: Splitting networks so a compromise or guest device cannot freely reach sensitive systems.
terms.context: Guest Wi-Fi without segmentation is a hallway into the building.

terms.title: Hidden SSID
terms.definition: Not broadcasting the network name — weak obscurity; determined clients and attackers can still discover it.

terms.title: MAC filtering
terms.definition: Allow/deny Wi-Fi by hardware address — easily spoofed; not a real access-control substitute.

terms.title: AP placement
terms.definition: Where access points sit and how loud they transmit — affects coverage, leakage outside the building, and attack surface.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — access point placement / power levels

terms.title: Wi-Fi analyzer
terms.definition: Tool that shows SSIDs, channels, signal strength, and sometimes security modes — useful for survey and spotting twins.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — wireless analyzers / site survey tools

terms.title: Bluetooth
terms.definition: Short-range wireless for peripherals and phones — convenient, and a side channel if pairing is careless.

terms.title: Bluejacking
terms.definition: Sending unsolicited messages to nearby Bluetooth devices — annoying spam more than full takeover.

terms.title: Bluesnarfing
terms.definition: Unauthorized access to data on a Bluetooth device — contacts, messages, files — when pairing/security is weak.

terms.title: Bluetooth pairing hygiene
terms.definition: Only pair expected devices, prefer confirm codes, turn discovery off when idle — desk-level Bluetooth risk control.
refs: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 — Bluetooth security practices

terms.title: Help desk
terms.definition: Front-line IT support that takes tickets, coaches users, and escalates security signals.

terms.title: Ticket
terms.definition: Tracked support request — the work unit the desk opens, updates, and closes.

terms.title: Access point (AP)
terms.definition: Device that bridges wireless clients onto the wired LAN — the radio end of corporate Wi-Fi.

terms.title: Wireless controller
terms.definition: Central brain that manages many APs — SSIDs, encryption mode, rogue detection, guest policy.

terms.title: VPN
terms.definition: Encrypted tunnel for traffic — still wise on untrusted Wi-Fi even when the café page looks friendly.

terms.title: Client/server certificate (Wi-Fi)
terms.definition: Credential material used in enterprise Wi-Fi so clients can verify the real RADIUS/network and not a twin.

terms.title: Signal strength
terms.definition: How loud the AP looks to a client — useful for coverage tickets and for noticing a twin that is 'too strong' in the wrong place.

terms.title: SOC
terms.definition: Security operations center — team that monitors alerts, investigates wireless attacks, and coordinates response.
